careerRoles.title: Full Stack Developer
careerRoles.description: Builds end-to-end web applications, designing interactive client frontends, scalable server APIs, and database architectures.

dailyResponsibilities: Architect and build responsive user interfaces in React or Next.js

Model and query relational and NoSQL databases with PostgreSQL and MongoDB

Deploy applications using Docker, CI/CD pipelines, and cloud hosting

careerRoles.title: AI/ML Engineer
careerRoles.description: Designs, trains, deploys, and monitors machine learning models and generative AI systems in production.
careerRoles.shortDescription: Train deep learning models, fine-tune LLMs, and deploy AI systems to production.
dailyResponsibilities: Process, clean, and engineer features from massive tabular, text, and image datasets
Train supervised and unsupervised models using PyTorch, TensorFlow, and Scikit-learn
Build RAG pipelines, prompt systems, and fine-tune LLM embeddings
Serve models with low latency using FastAPI, Triton, or ONNX runtime
Monitor model drift, hallucination metrics, and inference costs

careerRoles.title: Data Analyst
careerRoles.description: Transforms raw business data into actionable dashboards, KPIs, statistical findings, and strategic recommendations.
careerRoles.shortDescription: Uncover business insights, query massive datasets, and craft compelling visual narratives.
dailyResponsibilities: Write complex SQL queries, window functions, and aggregations across enterprise data warehouses
Create interactive executive dashboards in Tableau, PowerBI, or Metabase
Perform exploratory data analysis and hypothesis testing in Python or R
Partner with cross-functional stakeholders to translate business questions into data models
Automate regular metrics reporting and anomaly detection pipelines

careerRoles.description: Combines computer science, predictive modeling, experimental design, and statistics to solve complex analytical problems.
careerRoles.shortDescription: Harness predictive statistics, A/B testing, and machine learning to build data-driven algorithms.

Build predictive classification, regression, and clustering algorithms in Python
Work with engineers to productionize data features and pipeline transformations
Present mathematical findings to executives with clear business impact statements

careerRoles.description: Architects, secures, deploys, and optimizes scalable multi-cloud infrastructure and distributed server architectures.

Configure VPCs, IAM policies, security groups, subnets, and routing tables
Optimize compute costs and establish high-availability multi-region failovers

careerRoles.title: Cybersecurity Analyst
careerRoles.description: Safeguards organizations against cyber threats, conducts vulnerability assessments, investigates security incidents, and enforces compliance.

Coordinate incident response protocols and forensic evidence collection

careerRoles.title: DevOps Engineer

questions.question: What is the difference between "==" and "===" in JavaScript?
options: They are completely identical and interchangeable
"==" checks value only with type coercion, while "===" checks value and type without coercion
"===" is used exclusively for comparing objects and arrays
"==" is faster than "===" in all JavaScript engines
questions.explanation: The double equals (==) operator performs abstract equality comparison with type coercion if the operands are of different types. The triple equals (===) operator performs strict equality comparison with no type coercion.

questions.question: What will be output to the console when the following code executes?
questions.explanation: Synchronous statements run first (1, 4). Then the microtask queue (Promise.then) runs before the macrotask queue (setTimeout callback), producing 1, 4, 3, 2.

questions.question: In JavaScript closures, what does an inner function retain access to?
options: Only global variables declared with var
Its own scope, the outer enclosing function's lexical scope, and the global scope
Only the parameters explicitly passed into the inner function
A cloned snapshot of primitive values at execution time
questions.explanation: A closure is the combination of a function bundled together with references to its surrounding state (the lexical environment). An inner function has access to variables in its own scope, its outer functions, and global scope.

questions.question: What does this JavaScript generator expression evaluate to?
options: undefined undefined
Throws an infinite loop memory error
questions.explanation: Generators execute lazily. Each call to gen.next() runs the generator function until the next yield statement, returning the value and pausing execution. The first call yields 1, and the second yields 2.

questions.question: Why should keys in React lists be unique and stable across renders?
options: To prevent CSS styles from clashing on adjacent list items
To help React identify which items have changed, been added, or been removed during reconciliation
React will throw a fatal compile-time syntax error without them
Keys are used by the browser to allocate DOM memory
questions.explanation: Keys provide a permanent identity to each element so React's virtual DOM diffing algorithm can accurately preserve component state and avoid re-rendering unmutated sibling nodes.

questions.question: What is the issue with this React useEffect implementation?
options: It has a memory leak because it does not return a cleanup function to clearInterval on unmount
The dependency array cannot be empty in React 18
setCount cannot accept a function argument
setInterval does not work inside useEffect
questions.explanation: Subscribing to timers or listeners inside useEffect must return a cleanup function (e.g., () => clearInterval(timer)) to prevent memory leaks and zombie intervals when the component unmounts.

questions.question: When is useMemo genuinely beneficial for performance optimization?
options: Wrap every single string and number variable in useMemo by default
When recalculating expensive computational operations or preserving referential equality for dependency arrays of child components wrapped in memo
Only when making asynchronous fetch API requests
It replaces the need for useState in functional components
questions.explanation: useMemo has memory and invocation overhead. It is beneficial when performing genuinely expensive calculations (e.g., sorting 10k items) or passing object/array references to memoized children to prevent unnecessary re-renders.

questions.question: What is the primary difference between a Python list and a tuple?
options: Tuples can hold strings while lists can only hold numbers
Lists are mutable (can be changed after creation), whereas tuples are immutable
Tuples are indexed from 1, whereas lists are indexed from 0
Lists cannot contain nested structures
questions.explanation: In Python, lists are mutable sequences defined with square brackets [], whereas tuples are immutable sequences defined with parentheses (), meaning items cannot be added, removed, or reassigned after instantiation.

questions.question: What does the following Python list comprehension produce?
questions.codeSnippet:
data = [1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6]
result = [x**2 for x in data if x % 2 == 0]
print(result)
questions.explanation: The condition "if x % 2 == 0" filters only even numbers from data (2, 4, 6). The expression x**2 squares each: 2^2=4, 4^2=16, 6^2=36.

questions.question: What is the role of the Global Interpreter Lock (GIL) in standard CPython?
options: It encrypts Python bytecode during compilation
It is a mutex that prevents multiple native threads from executing Python bytecodes at once
It prevents files from being modified by two processes simultaneously
It limits Python programs to using a maximum of 4GB of RAM
questions.explanation: The GIL is a mechanism used by CPython to ensure thread-safe memory management. It allows only one OS thread to execute Python bytecode at a time, which is why multiprocessing or C extensions are typically used for CPU-bound parallelism.

questions.question: What is the difference between WHERE and HAVING clauses in SQL?
options: WHERE and HAVING are completely identical aliases
WHERE filters rows before aggregation, while HAVING filters aggregated groups created by GROUP BY
HAVING only works on integer primary keys
WHERE is only supported in SQLite, not PostgreSQL
questions.explanation: The WHERE clause filters individual records before any grouping takes place. The HAVING clause filters the summarized groups that result from a GROUP BY clause.

questions.question: What will this SQL query return?
questions.codeSnippet:
SELECT department, AVG(salary) as avg_sal
FROM employees
GROUP BY department
HAVING AVG(salary) > 80000;
options: All employees who individually earn more than 80,000
Departments where the average salary among employees exceeds 80,000 along with their average salary
The highest paid department and its minimum salary
A syntax error because AVG cannot be placed in the HAVING clause
questions.explanation: The query groups all rows by department, calculates the average salary for each department, and then filters to include only those departments whose average salary is strictly greater than 80,000.

questions.question: In database transaction processing, what does the "I" in ACID stand for and guarantee?
options: Indexing: Ensures all columns have B-tree indices
Isolation: Ensures concurrent execution of transactions leaves the database in the same state as if executed sequentially
Iteration: Guarantees recursive queries terminate
Immutability: Disallows updating historical records
questions.explanation: Isolation guarantees that transactions are isolated from each other so that concurrent transactions do not observe intermediate, uncommitted states, preventing phenomena like dirty reads and phantom reads.

questions.question: What is the command to create a new branch named "feature-login" and switch to it in Git?
options: git new branch feature-login
git checkout -b feature-login (or git switch -c feature-login)
git branch --switch feature-login
git merge feature-login
questions.explanation: Both "git checkout -b <name>" and the modern "git switch -c <name>" create the specified branch and immediately point HEAD to it.

questions.question: What is the primary difference between a Docker Image and a Docker Container?
options: An image is a running process, while a container is a compiled binary file
An image is a read-only template with instructions, while a container is a runnable, isolated instance of an image
Containers can only run on Linux, while images can only run on Windows
Images require a hypervisor, while containers do not
questions.explanation: A Docker image is an immutable, layered blueprint containing application code, runtime, libraries, and dependencies. A container is a live, running instance of an image with a thin writable container layer.

questions.question: What is the average time complexity for searching an element in a Hash Map?
options: O(n)
O(log n)
O(n log n)
questions.explanation: Hash maps compute the bucket index using a hash function, providing O(1) constant average time complexity for lookups, insertions, and deletions under good hashing distribution.

questions.question: Which sorting algorithm has a worst-case time complexity of O(n log n) and guarantees stable ordering?
options: Quick Sort
Merge Sort
Heap Sort
Selection Sort
questions.explanation: Merge Sort uses a divide-and-conquer strategy that consistently runs in O(n log n) time across best, average, and worst cases, and is stable (preserves relative order of equal elements).
